hints.content:
The function $f$ is positive $($i.e. $f(x)>0)$ whenever its graph is above the $x$-axis.

This is because the positive $y$-values are above the $x$-axis, and $y=f(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of the function y equals f of x is below the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative four and one-half. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative four and one-half to x equals negative two and one-quarter. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative two and one-quarter to x equals zero. It is above the x-axis from x equals zero to x equals three and one-half. It is below the x-axis after x equals three and one-half. The function is increasing from x equals negative five to x equals negative three and one-half. The function is decreasing from x equals negative three and one-half to x equals negative one. The function increases from x equals negative one to x equals two and one-half. The function decreases indefinitely after x equals two and one-half. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative four and one-half to x equals negative two and one-quarter and from x equals zero to x equals three and one-half.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $-4<x<-3$.
